title: Spark shuffle internals: the write path, the read path, and why it pins executors
purpose: Spark shuffle internals. Wide transformation forces redistribution; Map task writes data and index files; MapOutputTracker holds block locations; Reduce task fetches blocks; Lost executor triggers stage recompute.
accessibleSummary: Spark shuffle internals. Wide transformation forces redistribution; Map task writes data and index files; MapOutputTracker holds block locations; Reduce task fetches blocks; Lost executor triggers stage recompute.
longDescription: Spark shuffle internals. Wide transformation forces redistribution; Map task writes data and index files; MapOutputTracker holds block locations; Reduce task fetches blocks; Lost executor triggers stage recompute.

nodes.label: Wide transformation
nodes.summary: A wide transformation forces redistribution and starts a new stage.
nodes.detail: A wide transformation forces redistribution and starts a new stage.
nodes.whyItMatters: A wide transformation forces redistribution and starts a new stage.

evidence.note: spark.sql.shuffle.partitions defaults to 200 and sets the partitions a shuffle produces.

inputs: A join, groupBy, distinct or repartition
processing: Cut a new stage at the exchange
outputs: Two stages separated by a shuffle
drill.example: A groupBy on order_date splits one job into a map stage and a reduce stage.
failureModes: Chaining many wide operations produces a shuffle storm, each a full network and disk barrier.

nodes.label: Map task writes its output
nodes.summary: Each map task writes one data file and one index file of partition offsets.
nodes.detail: Each map task writes one data file and one index file of partition offsets.
nodes.whyItMatters: Each map task writes one data file and one index file of partition offsets.

evidence.note: An executor writes its map output locally to disk and then serves those files to other executors.

processing: Write a data file and an index file
drill.example: A task producing 200 output partitions writes one data file and one index of 200 offsets.
failureModes: Local disk exhaustion fails the task outright.

nodes.label: …to executor-local disk
nodes.summary: Shuffle output is written once to executor-local disk with no replica.
nodes.detail: Shuffle output is written once to executor-local disk with no replica.
nodes.whyItMatters: Shuffle output is written once to executor-local disk with no replica.

evidence.note: Shuffle data written to each executor's local disk prevents release until downstream stages finish reading.

processing: Persist to the executor's own disk
drill.example: One executor holds the only copy of the blocks forty reducers will need.
controls: Remote shuffle storage removes this dependency
failureModes: Losing the executor loses the only copy of its shuffle output.

nodes.label: MapOutputTracker
nodes.summary: The driver's MapOutputTracker maps shuffle partitions to block locations.
nodes.detail: The driver's MapOutputTracker maps shuffle partitions to block locations.
nodes.whyItMatters: The driver's MapOutputTracker maps shuffle partitions to block locations.

evidence.note: Shuffle block locations must be resolvable for a reduce task to fetch its input.

processing: Record shuffle and partition to block manager mapping
drill.example: Reduce partition 37 resolves to the block manager on executor 4.
controls: Driver memory holds the tracker state
failureModes: Very high shuffle partition counts inflate tracker metadata on the driver.

nodes.label: Reduce task fetches blocks
nodes.summary: Reduce tasks fetch their blocks in parallel from every producing executor.
nodes.detail: Reduce tasks fetch their blocks in parallel from every producing executor.
nodes.whyItMatters: Reduce tasks fetch their blocks in parallel from every producing executor.

evidence.note: Executors fetch shuffle files from each other unless an external shuffle service serves them.

drill.example: A reducer pulls its slice from 40 producing executors concurrently.
failureModes: A saturated producer becomes a straggler for every reducer needing it.

nodes.label: So the producer cannot be released
nodes.summary: An executor holding unread shuffle output cannot be safely released.
nodes.detail: An executor holding unread shuffle output cannot be safely released.
nodes.whyItMatters: An executor holding unread shuffle output cannot be safely released.

evidence.note: Dynamic allocation removing an executor before a shuffle is consumed forces unnecessary recomputation.
Shuffle data on local disk prevents executor release until downstream stages finish reading.

inputs: An executor with no running tasks
drill.example: An executor sits idle for minutes holding blocks a later stage has not yet fetched.
failureModes: Elastic scaling is defeated: you pay for idle compute purely to protect data.

nodes.label: Remove it anyway → stage recompute
nodes.summary: A failed fetch recomputes the entire owning stage, not one partition.
nodes.detail: A failed fetch recomputes the entire owning stage, not one partition.
nodes.whyItMatters: A failed fetch recomputes the entire owning stage, not one partition.

evidence.note: Losing an executor holding shuffle data raises FetchFailedException and forces re-execution of the affected stage.

drill.example: One lost executor forces a 12-minute map stage to run a second time.
failureModes: Repeated losses cause a retry storm where stages re-run faster than they complete.

nodes.label: The bond to break
nodes.summary: Shuffle output living and dying with its executor is the bond to break.
nodes.detail: Shuffle output living and dying with its executor is the bond to break.
nodes.whyItMatters: Shuffle output living and dying with its executor is the bond to break.

evidence.note: Efficient Scaledown decouples shuffle data from executor lifetime.

drill.example: An executor cannot leave because it is the only holder of its shuffle blocks.
failureModes: Without any mitigation, scale-down is either blocked or unsafe.

nodes.label: Shuffle tracking
nodes.summary: Shuffle tracking keeps executors holding needed shuffle data alive.
nodes.detail: Shuffle tracking keeps executors holding needed shuffle data alive.
nodes.whyItMatters: Shuffle tracking keeps executors holding needed shuffle data alive.

evidence.note: Shuffle tracking keeps executors holding needed shuffle data rather than removing them.

processing: Retain executors still holding needed shuffle data
drill.example: An executor is exempted from removal while its blocks remain unread.
failureModes: It preserves correctness but still pays for idle compute.

nodes.label: External shuffle service
nodes.summary: An external shuffle service serves shuffle files beyond the executor's lifetime.
nodes.detail: An external shuffle service serves shuffle files beyond the executor's lifetime.
nodes.whyItMatters: An external shuffle service serves shuffle files beyond the executor's lifetime.

evidence.note: With an external shuffle service, shuffle state written by an executor continues to be served beyond that executor's lifetime.

processing: Serve blocks from a separate service
outputs: Shuffle state that outlives the executor
drill.example: Executors fetch from the service rather than from the process that produced the data.
failureModes: The service itself becomes shared infrastructure to operate and scale.

nodes.label: Graceful decommissioning
nodes.summary: Graceful decommissioning migrates blocks to a peer before the executor exits.
nodes.detail: Graceful decommissioning migrates blocks to a peer before the executor exits.
nodes.whyItMatters: Graceful decommissioning migrates blocks to a peer before the executor exits.

evidence.note: Graceful decommissioning migrates shuffle blocks to a peer or fallback storage before the executor exits; both properties default to false.

processing: Migrate blocks to a peer or fallback storage
drill.example: Blocks move to a peer executor over the network before the source node terminates.
failureModes: Both settings default to false, so the protection is absent unless deliberately enabled.

edges.label: Stage boundary triggers the map-side write
Data and index files land on local disk
Block locations are reported to the driver
Pending fetches keep the producer alive
Removing it anyway forces a stage recompute
